main_text.head: Argumentum & usus historiae re-gum Israelis & Juda,

p.i: Scinditur infælix fatali scismate regnum, Hinc varia Regum perpetuaq; vices. Corrupti mores populi, vatumq; labores, Et scelerum pœnæ, bella cruenta, fames. Caca superstitio, venalia iura, tyrannis, Atq; libido vagans, luxus, avaritia. Occisi multo divini sanguine vates, Et contempta Dei numina sancta patris. Exitium regno miserabile utriq; dederunt, Sic vitiis periit gens populosa suis. Corruit Israel, mox urbs pugnacis Juda, Cum templo infælix facta ruina iacet. Salva tamen semper victrix Ecclesia mansit, Perpetuo æterni tuta favore Dei. Atq; suo venit promissus tempore CHRISTUS, Integer ex casta virgine factus homo. Discite iustitiam Reges, CHRISTUMQUE vereri[?], Illius & facili subdite colla iugo. Discite cultores CHRISTI, non nulla timere, Quæ vobis reges dira pericla struunt. Vivit adhuc CHRISTUS, vivet, regnabit & usq;, Nec, quos asseruit, deseruisse potest.

page.notes: No page number, running head, catchword or signature is printed. The title "Argumentum" is a level 2 heading over the verse. "vereri" is read from a worn line and is doubtful, so it is marked [?]; the sense suggests "venerari". The first letter of the verse is a large initial "S" joined to "cinditur". "Quæ" in the last-but-one verse line is doubtful as to the æ ligature. The faint text above the title is show-through from the other side and is not transcribed.
